package.question: Does Method M (and its calibrated variant Method M+) give larger certified robustness to edit-distance perturbations than fixed-rate smoothing baselines, consistently across text classification datasets, and at what cost in clean accuracy?
package.methods_summary: Method M is a randomized-smoothing certification method for text classifiers against edit-distance attacks. At prediction time, tokens of the input are randomly deleted and a base classifier votes over many deleted copies; unlike the fixed-rate deletion baseline CERT-ED, Method M lets the deletion rate depend on input length (parameters: a lower bound on the deletion probability and a length constant), and the paper derives a matching certificate. Method M+ further sets the rate per length bin using an empirical calibration on the training set. RanMASK masks a fixed fraction of tokens and certifies only Hamming distance.
package.experimental_setup: Base model: pretrained RoBERTa, fine-tuned with the same procedure for all smoothed models; NoSmooth is the plain classifier. Datasets: Yelp five-class sentiment (10,000 sampled test reviews), SpamAssassin spam detection, and LUN unreliable-news detection. Inference uses 1,000 Monte Carlo samples for prediction and 4,000 for certification. Metrics: clean accuracy; certified radius (CR, set to 0 for misclassified inputs); log10 cardinality of the certified region (CC); and a Wasserstein distance measuring how CR tracks input length.

experiments.description: Certified robustness vs clean accuracy on Yelp (5-class sentiment), SpamAssassin (spam) and LUN (unreliable news) (T1, T2)

comparisons.description: Method M and Method M+ vs CERT-ED and RanMASK: mean certified radius and certified-region cardinality per dataset
Clean-accuracy cost of certification: smoothed models vs NoSmooth, and Method M/M+ vs CERT-ED
Adaptation to input length (Wasserstein distance) across methods

results_tables.caption: Clean accuracy (%) and mean certified radius (Mean CR, ± standard error across test examples) for RoBERTa-based classifiers on three datasets. Percentages after RanMASK / CERT-ED / Method M give the masking or deletion rate setting; NoSmooth has no certificate.
results_tables.notes: Restructured from the source's appendix certificate table (one block per dataset); values verbatim, bold not reproduced. '---' = not applicable. A further block labelled 'Yelp' a second time (apparently a different dataset) was not used because its label is ambiguous. Standard errors reflect variability across test examples for a single trained model; no repeated training runs or significance tests are reported.

results_tables.caption: Aggregate log10 cardinality of the certified region (median; first quartile for Yelp, where the median is zero) and Wasserstein distance between standardized distributions of certified radius and input length (smaller = better adaptation to input length).
results_tables.notes: Same source table as T1. For RanMASK log(CC) is an exact count under Hamming distance; for the deletion-based methods it is a lower bound under edit distance (underestimating by at most one order of magnitude, per the source).
